successors.note: Cliopatria keeps Babur's realm in its Timurid row to 1528 and starts the Mughal Empire only in 1529. The Timurid main branches had ended earlier: the Uzbeks took Samarkand and Bukhara in 1501 (shaybanids) and Herat in 1507.

capitals.name: Herat
capitals.note: Infobox: Herat 1405-1447; Shah Rukh ruled from Herat (governor of Khorasan from 1397).

capitals.name: Samarkand
capitals.note: Infobox gives Samarkand 1447-1459 (Ulugh Beg, then Abu Sa'id from 1451); the Abu Sa'id page has him make Herat his capital after re-annexing Khorasan in 1458.

capitals.name: Herat
capitals.note: Infobox: Herat 1459-1507; Husayn Bayqara ruled it 1469-1506. After 1469 the Timurid princes of Samarkand, Hissar, Fergana and Kabul ruled their own seats.

capitals.name: Kabul
capitals.note: Babur took Kabul in October 1504 and 'would remain its ruler until 1526'; it is the seat of the surviving Timurid line after Herat fell in 1507.

rulers.name: Timur (Tamerlane)
rulers.note: Infobox: 1370-1405; the Timur page gives his coronation as 9 April 1370 and his death at Farab on 17 or 18 February 1405.

rulers.name: Shah Rukh
rulers.note: Ruled from Herat from 1405; 'took the throne in 1409' after the civil war (Timur page); died 13 March 1447. Khalil Sultan was a rival emperor at Samarkand 1405-1409.

rulers.name: Ulugh Beg
rulers.note: Shah Rukh's son; murdered in 1449 by his son Abdal-Latif.

rulers.name: Abu Sa'id Mirza
rulers.note: Took Samarkand in June 1451, Herat by 1458; executed 5 February 1469. 1449-1451 was civil war (Abdal-Latif, Abdullah Mirza).

rulers.name: Husayn Bayqara (Herat)
rulers.note: Took Herat on 24 March 1469 and held it to 4 May 1506. Parallel Timurid lines in the same years: Sultan Ahmad at Samarkand 1469-1494, Mahmud at Hissar and Badakhshan, Umar Shaikh II in Fergana, Ulugh Beg II at Kabul (Abu Sa'id page).

rulers.name: Badi' al-Zaman
rulers.note: Last ruler in the infobox (1506-1507); with Muzaffar Husain he inherited Herat, which the Uzbeks took in 1507.

rulers.name: Babur (Kabul)
rulers.note: Ruler of Kabul 1504-1526, 'assumed the title of Padshah among the Timurids'; founds the Mughal Empire at Panipat on 21 April 1526.

Cliopatria starts this shape in 1502, but the Uzbeks took Bukhara and Samarkand in 1501 (Muhammad Shaybani page; 'In 1501 the Uzbeks conquered Transoxiana from Abu Sa'id's grandson, Babur', Husayn Bayqara page) and Babur's attempt to recapture Samarkand and Fergana failed that year. What remains is Husayn Bayqara's Khorasan; Kabul is still outside until October 1504. [fx-15] also without Pakistani Punjab and Multan (the Punjab leaves in 1407 (ledger 23) and the Langah Sultanate page has Multan 'independent of the Sultanate of Delhi' after Timur's 1398 invasion, its people choosing Shaikh Yousaf Qureshi in 1438 and Rai Sahra of the Langahs taking it in 1445; the Timurid Empire and Langah pages give the Timurids no hold on Multan or the Punjab after 1399).

minus.text: the 1502 shape plus Kabul province (Babur's mountain kingdom)
Pakistani Punjab and the Multan country

correction.text: the 1502 shape plus Kabul province (Babur's mountain kingdom); also without Pakistani Punjab and Multan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1504-1506: 'In October 1504, Babur was able to cross the snowy Hindu Kush mountains and capture Kabul'. Husayn Bayqara died on 4 May 1506 (his page) and Herat passed to Badi' al-Zaman and Muzaffar Husain. [fx-15] also without Pakistani Punjab and Multan (the Punjab leaves in 1407 (ledger 23) and the Langah Sultanate page has Multan 'independent of the Sultanate of Delhi' after Timur's 1398 invasion, its people choosing Shaikh Yousaf Qureshi in 1438 and Rai Sahra of the Langahs taking it in 1445; the Timurid Empire and Langah pages give the Timurids no hold on Multan or the Punjab after 1399).

correction.text: unchanged: Babur's Kabul, valid 1507-1510

keyframe_review.note: Valid 1507-1510: 117,000 km2 round Kabul and Ghazni, Babur's realm after the Uzbeks 'took Herat, the southern capital of the Timurids' in 1507 (Muhammad Shaybani page). Samarkand was taken again in 1511, so the shape holds to 1510.

correction.text: Kabul plus Samarkand and Bukhara for the one year of Babur's third reign there

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1511: 'in 1511, after leaving his brother Nasir Mirza to rule Kabul, he managed to take Samarkand for the third time'; he 'lost Samarkand and Bukhara again in 1512'.

correction.text: use the 1507 shape (Kabul and Ghazni) for 1512-1515: Samarkand and Bukhara were lost in 1512

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws 964,685 km2 (Samarkand, Bukhara, Fergana, Balkh and Kabul) for 1512-1515, but the Babur page loses Samarkand and Bukhara in 1512 and gives him only Kabul until his Indian conquests; the shape is a year late and 4 years too long, and Fergana is not on the page.

correction.text: unchanged, valid 1516-1521

keyframe_review.note: Valid 1516-1521: Kabul and the Badakhshan side (Babur took 'control of Badakhshan after the death of Uways Mirza' in 1521). Kandahar is annexed in 1522, which this shape lacks.

correction.text: the 1516 shape plus Kandahar

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1522-1524: 'In 1522, he besieged and annexed Kandahar from the Arghun dynasty'.

minus.text: the 1522 shape plus the Punjab (Lahore)
Multan, the Langah Sultanate's country

correction.text: the 1522 shape plus the Punjab (Lahore); also without Multan, the Langah Sultanate's country until 1528

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1525: 'Babur started for Lahore in 1524' and by 1525 had become 'the master of Punjab' within three weeks of crossing the Indus. [fx-15] also without Multan, the Langah Sultanate's country until 1528 (Langah page: Multan 'fell in 1528' to the Arghuns).

minus.text: unchanged shape, years 1526-1528 transferred to the Mughal Empire
Multan, the Langah Sultanate's country

correction.text: unchanged shape, years 1526-1528 transferred to the Mughal Empire; also without Multan, the Langah Sultanate's country until 1528

keyframe_review.note: Babur wins the First Battle of Panipat on 21 April 1526 and 'founded the Mughal Empire'. The shape (606,000 km2: Kabul, Kandahar, Punjab) is Babur's realm and stays as drawn, but it belongs to mughal-empire from 1526, not to the Timurids; Cliopatria's own Mughal row starts only in 1529, so the mughal-empire dossier (sa-0x) should draw 1526-1528 from this shape. [fx-15] also without Multan, the Langah Sultanate's country until 1528 (Langah page: Multan 'fell in 1528' to the Arghuns).

ledger.note: 1370: Timur is proclaimed sovereign at Balkh and rules Transoxiana. The Timur page says he was 'formally proclaimed sovereign at Balkh' with the infobox coronation 9 April 1370; the Timurid Empire page has him take Samarkand in 1366 and Balkh in 1369 and be 'recognized as ruler' of Transoxiana in 1370. The pages give cities, not a boundary.

region.text: Herat and Khorasan, Sistan to the south

ledger.note: 1383: Timur begins the conquest of Persia at Herat. 'In 1383, Timur started his lengthy military conquest of Persia' beginning with Herat; he 'ruled much of Khorasan by 1381' and the Timurid Empire page has him remove the Kartids 'by 1389'. Cliopatria's Kartid row ends 1384 and its Timurid shape takes in Khorasan in 1385.

region.text: Kandahar and Helmand, Baluchistan and the Pakistan fringe

ledger.note: 1385: the rest of the eastern lands are Timurid on Cliopatria's map. Page silent: Cliopatria's 1385 shape adds Kandahar, Helmand, Baluchistan and the Pakistan fringe to its 1375 shape, none of which the Timur or Timurid Empire pages name or date (the Timur page has Khorasan by 1381 and the Persian war from 1383); bridging judgment of the year.
1387: Timur takes Isfahan. 'the city immediately surrendered' and was massacred after a revolt. The page does not name Isfahan's holder; the Muzaffarids ruled central Persia (annexed in 1393).

region.text: Fars with Shiraz, and the Muzaffarid Kerman and Gulf coast

ledger.note: 1393: Shiraz falls and the Muzaffarids are annexed. 'Shiraz was captured after surrendering' and 'the Muzafarids were annexed'; the Timurid Empire page: 'Removes the Muzaffarids at Shiraz'. Kerman is my reading of the Muzaffarid lands.

region.text: western and northern Iran, Azerbaijan, Armenia and the Caucasus fringe

ledger.note: 1395: the west of the plateau and the Caucasus are Timurid on Cliopatria's map. Page silent on the takeover of Azerbaijan, Armenia, Tehran, Hamadan, Khuzestan and the Turkmen and Caucasus fringe (4,999 cells beyond the 1393 keyframe). The Timurid Empire page lists 1394-1395 'Triumphs over the Golden Horde after Georgia campaign' and the Timur page the Georgian raids of 1386 and 1394; Cliopatria draws the Qara Qoyunlu and Jalayirid cores separately until 1401. Bridging judgment.

region.text: Delhi and the Doab round it

ledger.note: December 1398: Timur enters Delhi. He 'Defeats Mahmud Shah; enters Delhi' (the battle was 17 December, Timur page) and the city was sacked; a raid, not an annexation.
January 1399: Timur leaves Delhi. The Timurid Empire page: '1399 (Jan.) Leaves Delhi'.

1400: Timur sacks Aleppo and Damascus. The Timur page dates both sacks to 1400 (infobox); the Timurid Empire page lists 'Conquers Aleppo, Damascus, eastern Anatolia' for 1400-1401. The pages do not say Timur kept the cities.

1401: the Syrian cities are left. Page silent on when Timur withdrew from Aleppo and Damascus; bridging judgment, the 1402 Cliopatria shape no longer shows Syria in the same strength and the next campaign is Ankara.

region.text: Baghdad and the Jalayirid lands in Iraq

ledger.note: June 1401: Timur takes Baghdad. 'Timur invaded Baghdad in June 1401'; the Timurid Empire page: 'Destroys Baghdad; expels the Jalayirids'. Cliopatria's Jalayirid shape of 1395-1401 (923 cells in Iraq) is absorbed into the Timurid 1402 shape.

1402: Khwarazm is Timurid on Cliopatria's map. Page silent on the date: the Timur page has 'five military campaigns against Khwarazm' and the siege of Urgench in 1379; the Timurid Empire page says only that Timur subjugated Khwarazm 'after 1370'. Cliopatria's Timurid shape holds Khwarezm only from 1402 (0.86 of the region); the golden-horde dossier (ia-02-a) records Khwarazm back under the Horde in 1383 and Timur's 1388 campaign, so this date is a floor, not the conquest.

minus.text: the steppe of southern Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan added in 1402

region.text: the steppe of southern Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan added in 1402 without the Kazakh steppe (Aqtobe)

ledger.note: 1402: the Aral and Syr Darya steppe joins Cliopatria's shape. Page silent; the golden-horde dossier (ia-02-a) records the same land leaving the Horde in 1402 for 'nobody' on Cliopatria's map. Bridging judgment. [fx-15: the Kazakh Steppe part (6 cells of Aqtobe, 45.3-45.7N 57.0-58.4E) is left out: the Abu'l-Khayr Khan and Kazakh Khanate pages have him subordinate 'most of the tribal confederations of the Eastern Desht-i Kipchak' in the 1420s-1450s and no page gives the Timurids this steppe.]

region.text: the Punjab and the Indian fringe of the 1402 shape

ledger.note: 1402: Cliopatria's shape adds the Punjab and an Indian fringe after Timur's 1398-1399 raid. Page silent: the pages give Delhi's sack and Timur's departure, not an annexation of the Punjab; bridging judgment of the date from Cliopatria's shape.

region.text: the Ottoman lands from Ankara to Smyrna

ledger.note: 20 July 1402: Timur defeats Bayezid at Ankara. 'defeated Bayezid in the Battle of Ankara on 20 July 1402' and 'In December 1402, Timur besieged and conquered Smyrna'. Cliopatria's 1402 shape draws Anatolia (0.32 of the region) as Timurid; the pages show a campaign, not a lasting annexation.

1403: Georgia becomes tributary. George VII pays tribute 'including 1,000 tankas of gold struck in the name of Timur' and 'Georgia became tributary to the Timurids', keeping independence as a Christian kingdom (the Truce of Shamkor of 1401 had earlier demanded troops). Cliopatria's vassalage relation runs 1395-1406.
1403: Anatolia is left. Page silent on Timur's withdrawal; the Georgia page has him at Birtvisi in August 1403 and at Beylagan in early 1404.

1405: Khalil Sultan seizes Samarkand. After Timur's death (17/18 February 1405, Timur page) 'Khalil Sultan proclaims himself emperor at Tashkent and seizes Samarqand'; Shah Rukh marches to the Oxus but does not attack. Khalil is a rival Timurid prince who held Transoxiana until 1409. [Counterpart was the string 'Khalil Sultan (rival Timurid emperor)'; now the khalil-sultan-and-rival-timurids dossier (orchestrator, 2 Nov 2026).]

1405: the capital passes to Herat. Infobox: Samarkand 1370-1405, Herat 1405-1447; Shah Rukh, governor of Khorasan since 1397, rules from Herat. Timur died at Farab in February 1405 on the march against Ming China.

region.text: Nakhchivan, Ganja and the Georgian lands

ledger.note: 1405: George VII recovers Nakhchivan and Ganja. After Timur's death 'he regained territory, including Nakhchivan and Ganja', and in 1406 defeated an Iranian army at Alatagh; the Georgia page gives no formal end of the tribute.
1405: Georgia's tribute lapses. The Georgia page notes only that 'Georgia's tribute and subordination weakened after Timur's death'; Cliopatria's vassalage ends 1406.

1405: Iraq slips away. Page silent on the exit from Iraq: the Qara Qoyunlu page has the Qara Qoyunlu capture Baghdad in 1410 and Qara Yusuf execute Shaykh Uways Jalayir at Tabriz, so Baghdad was not Timurid by then; bridging judgment of the year from Timur's death.

14 October 1406: Qara Yusuf retakes Tabriz. He 'defeats the Timurid Abu Bakr at Nakhchivan and reoccupies Tabriz'; on 20 April 1408 he beats Abu Bakr and Miran Shah at Sardrud, where Miran Shah is killed.

region.text: the Punjab and the Indian fringe

ledger.note: 1407: the Punjab leaves the Timurid shape. Page silent on any Timurid hold on the Punjab and on its end; Cliopatria drops it in 1407.

region.text: Khuzestan, Gilan and the north Caucasus fringe

ledger.note: 1407-1415: Khuzestan, Gilan and the north Caucasus fringe leave Cliopatria's shape. Page silent; the Qara Qoyunlu page has Iraq and the Gulf coast in Qara Qoyunlu hands after 1447, not before. Bridging judgment: the part of the 1407 shape beyond the 1415 shape that no other event names.

20 April 1408: Sardrud ends the Timurid hold on Tabriz. The Qara Qoyunlu page: 'Qara Yusuf inflicted a decisive defeat on them at the Battle of Sardrud' (Miran Shah killed), after he 'recovered Tabriz after defeating Abu Bakr' in 1406. The qara-qoyunlu contest over Tabriz (1406-1408) ended without a transfer of land, so the Timurid keyframes kept the Tabriz district drawn Timurid in 1410 (conflict_places, 119 cells). Mirror of the qara-qoyunlu gain (fx-15, F157).

1409: Shah Rukh takes Samarkand. 'He later takes Samarqand unopposed after Khalil Sultan is captured'; the war 'began to turn in Shah Rukh's favour' in 1409. Ulugh Beg is made governor of Transoxiana after 1411. [Counterpart was the string 'Khalil Sultan (rival Timurid emperor)'; now the khalil-sultan-and-rival-timurids dossier (orchestrator, 2 Nov 2026).]

region.text: Azerbaijan, Armenia and Qara Qoyunlu Iraq

ledger.note: 1420: Shah Rukh attacks the Qara Qoyunlu. Qara Yusuf died in November 1420 during the first Azerbaijan campaign, 'which ends in Timurid capture of Azerbaijan and Armenia'; Tabriz was occupied briefly in 1421; a second campaign in 1429 and a third in 1434.

region.text: Azerbaijan, Armenia and Qara Qoyunlu Iraq

ledger.note: 1434-1435: the third Azerbaijan expedition succeeds. 'Shah Rukh's third expedition succeeds. He entrusts the government to Iskander's brother, Jahan Shah, as a vassal.'

region.text: the Qara Qoyunlu lands under Jahan Shah

ledger.note: 1435: Jahan Shah rules the Qara Qoyunlu as Shah Rukh's vassal. Cliopatria's vassalage relation runs 1407-1467, but the page makes it a vassal only from the 1434-35 expedition to Shah Rukh's death in 1447 (Jahan Shah crowned 19 April 1438).

region.text: the Syr Darya lands round Sighnaq

ledger.note: 1446: Abu'l-Khayr Khan takes the Syr Darya. He 'invaded the Syr Darya region and took some lands from Timurid control. Sighnaq became his new capital' (Abu'l-Khayr page); the khanate-of-sibir dossier carries the matching gain. Cliopatria's Timurid shapes of 1440-1449 do not show these lands, so no keyframe change follows. [fx-15 review: counterpart re-pointed from khanate-of-sibir to uzbek-khanate-of-abul-khayr, the dossier of Abu'l-Khayr's realm, whose 1446 gain from timurid-empire is the mirror (fx-15 handed off the duplicate Sibir gain).]
1447: Jahan Shah becomes independent. 'After Shah Rukh dies, Jahan Shah becomes independent and adopts the titles sultan and khan' (Shah Rukh died 13 March 1447 at Rayy, Shah Rukh page).

1447: the Qara Qoyunlu take western Iran. 'Qara Qoyunlu annex parts of Iraq and the eastern Arabian coast, and take Timurid-held western Iran, including Sultaniya, Hamadan, and Qazvin'; the Timurid Empire page: they 'drive the Timurids to eastern Iran'.
1447: the seat moves to Samarkand. Infobox: Samarkand 1447-1459. Ulugh Beg briefly occupies Herat in 1448 and is murdered by his son in 1449 (Shah Rukh page).

1449: Abdal-Latif Mirza seizes Samarkand. 'Abdal-Latif then defeats and kills Ulugh Beg'; Abu Sa'id attacks Samarkand, is captured and escapes in 1450 to Bukhara. A dynastic war, not a foreign loss. [Counterpart was the string 'Abdal-Latif Mirza (Timurid rival)'; now the khalil-sultan-and-rival-timurids dossier (orchestrator, 2 Nov 2026).]

region.text: Khwarazm and the Syr Darya steppe

ledger.note: 1450: Khwarazm and the Syr Darya steppe leave Cliopatria's shape. Page silent on who took them; the Abu Sa'id page names the Uzbek ruler Abu'l-Khayr Khan only as the ally who helped him take Samarkand in June 1451. Bridging judgment.

June 1451: Abu Sa'id takes Samarkand. With the Uzbek Abu'l-Khayr Khan's help he 'defeats Abdullah Mirza and takes Samarqand, where he claims the throne'. The Timurid Empire page: 1451-1469 he 'briefly reunites most of the empire'. [Counterpart was the string 'Abdullah Mirza (Timurid rival)'; now the khalil-sultan-and-rival-timurids dossier (orchestrator, 2 Nov 2026).]

region.text: Saveh, Qum, Isfahan, Shiraz and Yazd, with the 1447 conquests

ledger.note: 1452-1453: Jahan Shah takes central and southern Iran. 'After the death of the Timurid governor of Fars, Jahan Shah takes Saveh, Qum, Isfahan, Shiraz, and Yazd' (page dates it 1452-53; 1453 here to match Cliopatria's shape break).
Summer 1458: Jahan Shah occupies Herat. He holds it 'for a few months' and withdraws because of his son's revolt and Abu Sa'id's march on Tabriz.
1458: Abu Sa'id re-annexes Khorasan. After Jahan Shah's withdrawal 'Abu Sa'id re-annex[ed] Khorasan and made Herat his capital'; he had captured Herat in 1456 after a long siege.
1459: Herat is the capital again. Infobox: Herat 1459-1507; the Abu Sa'id page has Herat his capital from 1458.

ledger.counterpart: Ala al-Dawla and Ibrahim Mirza (Timurid princes)
ledger.note: 1459: Abu Sa'id wins at Sarakhs and extends his rule. He defeats Sultan Sanjar, Ibrahim Mirza and Ala al-Dawla there and 'extends his rule toward Mazandaran and Sistan'; Husayn Bayqara occupied Mazandaran in 1460.

1463 (bridging year): Kerman passes to the Qara Qoyunlu. The Jahan Shah page says he took 'Savah, Qumm, Isfahan, Shiraz and Yazd' in 1452-1453 and 'even eventually Kerman' (undated), and has 'Qasim Beg was assigned to Kerman' in the account of the rebellions after 1458; the Qara Qoyunlu page repeats 'Qasim beg was assigned to Kerman'. 1463 is the year of the qara-qoyunlu keyframe that adds Kerman; the Timurid shapes of 1453-1462 (Cliopatria, Timurid to 1474) stand until then. Mirror of the qara-qoyunlu gain (fx-15, F157).

region.text: Azerbaijan from Miyana to the Araxes

ledger.note: February 1468: Abu Sa'id marches on the Aq Qoyunlu. After learning that Uzun Hasan had killed Jahan Shah, he launches a campaign 'as far as Miyana and the Araxes'.

region.text: Azerbaijan from Miyana to the Araxes

ledger.note: 5 February 1469: Abu Sa'id is beaten at Qarabagh and executed. He 'suffers a disastrous defeat at Qarabagh, is captured, and is executed by Yadgar Muhammad Mirza'. No Timurid land is gained or lost on the frontier.

24 March 1469: Husayn Bayqara takes Herat; the empire divides. He 'besieged Herat which he finally captured on March 24, 1469'. The Abu Sa'id page gives the partition: Sultan Ahmad at Samarkand, Mahmud at Badakhshan and Hissar, Umar Shaikh II in Fergana, Ulugh Beg II at Kabul and Ghazni; the Timurid Empire page says the territories were 'permanently divided'. The state continues as the dynasty's principalities; Herat's border with the Aq Qoyunlu runs from the southern Caspian to Lake Hamun.

region.text: Samarkand, Bukhara and Fergana, with the Hissar and Tokharistan fringe that Cliopatria's 1497 shape holds beyond its 1502 shape

ledger.note: 1501: the Uzbeks take Transoxiana. 'Shaybani ousted the Timurids from their capital Samarkand in 1500'; 'in 1501 he recaptured Samarkand' and 'conquered Bukhara in 1501'; Babur's 1501 attempt to retake Samarkand and Fergana failed (Babur page). Fergana was lost to Babur's rivals in 1497 and to the Uzbeks by 1503 (Battle of Akhsi).

ledger.counterpart: Kabul (previous holder not named on the page)
ledger.note: October 1504: Babur captures Kabul. 'In October 1504, Babur was able to cross the snowy Hindu Kush mountains and capture Kabul', which he ruled to 1526. The page does not name the previous holder (the Arghun dynasty is named only for Kandahar in 1522).

region.text: Herat, Khorasan and the Afghan lands round Balkh and Kandahar

ledger.note: 1507: the Uzbeks take Herat. 'In 1507 [Shaybani] also took Herat, the southern capital of the Timurids' (the Timurid Empire page: 'Uzbeks take Herat, ending the main Timurid branches'). Husayn Bayqara had died on 4 May 1506; his sons Badi' al-Zaman and Muzaffar Husain disputed the inheritance.
1507: the seat is Kabul. Babur holds Kabul from October 1504 and 'would remain its ruler until 1526'; after Herat's fall it is the Timurid seat.
1511: Babur takes Samarkand a third time. 'in 1511, after leaving his brother Nasir Mirza to rule Kabul, he managed to take Samarkand for the third time'.
1512: Samarkand and Bukhara are lost again. 'He lost Samarkand and Bukhara again in 1512.'
1521: Babur takes Badakhshan. 'In 1521, he took control of Badakhshan after the death of Uways Mirza.'
1522: Babur annexes Kandahar. 'In 1522, he besieged and annexed Kandahar from the Arghun dynasty.'

1525: Babur is master of the Punjab. He 'started for Lahore in 1524' and by 1525 was 'the master of Punjab' within three weeks of crossing the Indus (Bajaur was taken in 1519, the Chenab reached in 1519). The page does not name the Punjab's holder; the Lodi governor at Lahore is my reading.

region.text: the Sultanate of Delhi round Delhi and Agra

ledger.note: 21 April 1526: Babur wins at Panipat. He 'defeated Ibrahim Lodi, the Sultan of Delhi, at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 and founded the Mughal Empire'; the battle began the day after Babur reached Panipat on 20 April.

region.text: Babur's Kabul, Kandahar and the Punjab

ledger.note: 1526: the Timurid line becomes the Mughal Empire. Babur, who 'assumed the title of Padshah among the Timurids', founds the Mughal Empire at Panipat; Cliopatria starts its Mughal row only in 1529 and keeps Babur's realm in its Timurid row to 1528. The Wikipedia article's own end is the fall of Herat in 1507.

wars.name: Timur's conquest of Persia

zones.text: Herat and Khorasan (from 1383), Isfahan (1387), Shiraz and the Muzaffarid lands (1393)

wars.outcome: Timur takes Herat and Khorasan from 1383, removes the Kartids by 1389, takes Isfahan in 1387 and Shiraz in 1393, annexing the Muzaffarids.
wars.note: 'In 1383, Timur started his lengthy military conquest of Persia', beginning with Herat; Sistan about 1386 (inferred by the page reading); Mazandaran is mentioned without a date.

wars.name: Tokhtamysh-Timur war
wars.outcome: Timur destroys Tokhtamysh on the Kondurcha in 1391 and at the Terek in 1395 and sacks Sarai and Astrakhan, but holds no Golden Horde land.
wars.note: Dated only 'in 1391' and 'In 1395' on the Timur page; the golden-horde dossier carries the month (April 1395) and the 1387 start.

wars.name: Timur's invasions of Georgia

zones.text: Georgia: Tbilisi (1386), the Darial approach (1394), the kingdom (1399-1400), Birtvisi (1403)

wars.outcome: After campaigns in 1386-87, 1394, 1399, 1400-01 and 1403 George VII accepts tribute; 'Georgia became tributary to the Timurids' but kept its independence.
wars.note: Tbilisi fell on 22 November 1386; the Truce of Shamkor of 1401; the tribute of 1403.

wars.name: Timur's invasion of India
wars.outcome: Timur defeats Mahmud Shah, sacks Delhi in December 1398 and leaves in January 1399 without annexing it.

wars.name: Timur's Syrian and Anatolian campaigns, Battle of Ankara
wars.outcome: Timur sacks Aleppo and Damascus (1400), destroys Baghdad (1401), defeats Bayezid at Ankara (20 July 1402) and takes Smyrna in December 1402; none of it is held.

wars.name: Timurid war of succession of 1405
wars.outcome: Khalil Sultan seizes Samarkand in 1405; Pir Muhammad is assassinated in 1407, Miran Shah killed in 1408; Shah Rukh takes Samarkand in 1409 and takes the throne.

wars.name: Shah Rukh's Azerbaijan campaigns against the Qara Qoyunlu
wars.outcome: Campaigns of 1420-21, 1429-31 and 1434 end with Jahan Shah installed as a Timurid vassal; Tabriz is held only briefly in 1421.
wars.note: The Qara Qoyunlu page dates the third expedition 1434-35.

wars.name: Qara Qoyunlu conquest of Timurid western and central Iran

zones.text: Sultaniya, Hamadan, Qazvin (1447); Saveh, Qum, Isfahan, Shiraz and Yazd (1452-53)

wars.outcome: Jahan Shah takes the west after Shah Rukh's death, central and southern Iran in 1452-53 and holds Herat for a few months in 1458.

wars.name: Abu Sa'id Mirza's campaign against the Aq Qoyunlu
wars.outcome: Abu Sa'id is defeated and captured at Qarabagh and executed on 5 February 1469; no territorial change on the frontier.

wars.name: Husayn Bayqara's struggle for Herat
wars.outcome: Husayn takes Herat on 24 March 1469, beats Yadgar Muhammad at Chenaran on 15 September 1469, loses Herat on 7 July 1470 and recovers it six weeks later.

wars.name: Uzbek conquest of Transoxiana and Khorasan
wars.outcome: Shaybani ousts the Timurids from Samarkand (1500), takes Bukhara (1501) and Herat (1507); he dies at Merv on 2 December 1510.

wars.name: Babur's conquests in Kabul and Hindustan
wars.outcome: Babur takes Kabul in 1504, Badakhshan in 1521, Kandahar in 1522, the Punjab by 1525 and wins at Panipat on 21 April 1526, founding the Mughal Empire.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontiers on the pages: steppe, mountain and desert edges throughout. The Amu Darya between Herat and Samarkand (truce of 1454, 'the Oxus' under Husayn Bayqara) and the Caspian-to-Lake-Hamun line with the Aq Qoyunlu are the firmest, still approximate.

notes:
Cliopatria row: one row, 'Timurid Empire' 1375-1528. It runs three states' worth of history: Timur's empire (1370-1405), the Persian-Khorasanian realm of Shah Rukh and his successors, and the Herat/Samarkand/Kabul principalities of 1469-1526 ending in Babur's Kabul. I keep one dossier (dynasty, one colour) and end it in 1526 at the founding of the Mughal Empire; the Wikipedia article ends the empire in 1507 (fall of Herat) and Cliopatria in 1528. The Mughal dossier (sa-0x) should take over 1526-1528.

Corrections to the Cliopatria shapes (see keyframe_review): 1385-1392 holds Fars and Kerman six years before the Muzaffarids fell; the 1402 shape includes Delhi, Syria and Anatolia (raids); 1407-1414 keeps Iraq, Azerbaijan and Armenia after the Qara Qoyunlu and Georgia recovered them; 1440-1474 keeps western and southern Iran after the Qara Qoyunlu took it in 1447-1453; 1475-1506 omits Samarkand, Hissar and Kabul, which stayed Timurid until 1501/1504; 1512-1515 draws Samarkand and Bukhara a year late (Babur held them only in 1511-1512).

Relations in the seed that the pages do not support: 'Allegiance of Jalayirid Sultanate to Timurid Empire 1375-1394' (the Timur page has Baghdad taken by surprise in August 1393 and again in June 1401, but says nothing of suzerainty before; no vassal event was written); 'Alliance between Golden Horde and Timurid Empire 1385-1401' (the Timur page has war with Tokhtamysh 1387-1395; no alliance event written); 'Vassalage of Kingdom of Georgia 1395-1406' (the Georgia page makes Georgia tributary only after 1403; written as vassal_start 1403, vassal_end 1405); 'Vassalage of Qara Qoyunlu 1407-1467' (the Qara Qoyunlu page: vassal only 1434/35-1447; written so).

Not settled / unverified, page budget (9 pages) used: (1) the Timurid takeover of Azerbaijan, Armenia and the Caucasus before 1401 (Tabriz 1386, Sultaniya, the Jalayirid and Qara Qoyunlu wars of 1393-1400) is not on any page opened: the 1395 keyframe is 'ok, unverified'; (2) the Khwarazm conquest date (1402 here at confidence 1; the golden-horde dossier carries 1383 and 1388 steps); (3) the Pakistan and Kyrgyz shares of the 1415-1474 shapes; (4) Fars, Kerman and Tehran after 1453 (the Qara Qoyunlu page names Fars, Isfahan, Yazd, Saveh, Qum but not Kerman or Rayy); (5) Sultan Ahmad's Samarkand and Mahmud's Hissar 1469-1500 and Kabul's holders 1469-1504 rest on the single partition sentence of the Abu Sa'id page; (6) the Timurid Empire page's capital dates (Samarkand 1447-1459) conflict with the Abu Sa'id page's Herat-from-1458; (7) the Khalil Sultan regime of 1405-1409 held Samarkand for four years as a rival emperor and would be a rebel-type dossier (counterpart 'Khalil Sultan (rival Timurid emperor)'); Abdal-Latif and Abdullah Mirza (1449-1451) are shorter. (8) The Aq Qoyunlu take-over of the plateau (1468-1475) is not mine to date: the Timurid 1453 loss covers what the Qara Qoyunlu page names.

Page oddities: 'Timur's_invasions_of_Georgia' loaded only with the unencoded apostrophe. The Timurid Empire page gives the Samarkand fall as 1501 in its infobox and text, Muhammad Shaybani's page has 1500 and 1501; both are recorded. Names the gazetteer lacks and I used: none new beyond 'Nakhchivan' and 'Khwarezm', which exist.

Rulers: the strip lists the Herat/Samarkand line from the pages opened, not the full Timurid list (no 'List of Timurid rulers' page was opened); gaps 1409 (Khalil), 1449-1451 (civil war).
